headlines.title: Wrong-way crash on Montague Expressway in Santa Clara leaves 2 dead
headlines.description: Two men died Wednesday in a fiery, wrong-way crash on Montague Expressway in Santa Clara, according to police. Santa Clara police officers responded at about 11:58 a.m. to a reported crash on Montague Expressway at the Lafayette Street overpass and found two mangled vehicles, a GMC SUV on its side and fully engulfed in flames and a Honda pickup truck, police said. Citing a preliminary investigation, police said a man behind the wheel of the SUV was driving the wrong way on northbound Montague Expressway when he slammed into the pickup truck, which was being driven by a man. Both men died at the scene, police said. Their identities will be released by the Santa Clara County Office of the Medical Examiner. Police said the man driving the SUV may have been speeding, but his exact speed wasn’t immediately known. Anyone who witnessed the crash is encouraged to call Traffic Investigator S. Ernst at 408-615-4764. Those wishing to remain nameless are instructed to leave a message on the police department’s anonymous tip line at 408-615-4TIP (4847).

headlines.title: Apple to lay off 147 employees from South Bay offices
headlines.description: Apple is laying off 147 employees – most of them software engineers – from its offices in Sunnyvale and Cupertino. The news came down on the same day Apple announced its next product launch event on Sept. 9 at its Cupertino headquarters. The company is expected to unveil new iPhones and Apple Watches. Apple CEO Tim Cook plans to step down Sept 1. Longtime Apple executive John Ternus will take over.

headlines.title: San Pedro Social reportedly closing after late-night permit denial
headlines.description: Another business in San Jose’s San Pedro Square is closing up shop. A co-owner of San Pedro Social says the venue will close following a vote earlier this week by San Jose leaders denying the business’ request for a late-night permit. The venue wanted to stay open until 2 a.m., according to The Mercury News. Council members reportedly cited multiple fights outside the venue as a reason for denying the permit. The reported closure comes on the heels of news that another business in the city’s popular entertainment district is slated to close. Last month, Sushi Confidential announced it would close its San Pedro Square restaurant to focus on its other South Bay locations. Sushi Confidential’s last day in San Pedro Square is Monday.

headlines.title: Fremont police search for hotel sexual assault suspect
headlines.description: Fremont police are asking for the public’s help finding a person of interest in an alleged sex assault at a hotel last week. Police officials didn’t say at which hotel the alleged assault took place but said it happened on Aug. 16 at 1:30 p.m. in the 40000 block of Lakeview Boulevard. The person of interest is described as a man with a medium complexion who is 40 to 50 years old and tall and thin, police said. His hair is dark with some gray, mid-neck to shoulder length and fell below his ears. He has light brown or green eyes and may have a mole or bump on the bridge of his nose. Police did not specify his race. The man is being sought for questioning and no charges have been filed at this time. Anyone with information about this case can contact Fremont Police Department’s Crimes Against Persons unit at 510-790-6900.

headlines.title: Port of Oakland announces $640M project to accommodate larger ships
headlines.description: A $640 million project is coming to the Port of Oakland with the goal of accommodating larger ships and improving cargo efficiency. Port officials and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers announced plans Thursday to transform the port’s turning basins by widening parts of the harbor. City leaders joined port and federal officials for the signing of a design agreement marking the start of the modernization effort. The Port of Oakland said the improvements will allow some of the world’s largest and most environmentally advanced vessels to safely and more efficiently maneuver through the port’s waterways. Oakland’s mayor said the project will also help sustain the city’s position as a “green innovation hub” as the port transitions toward zero-emissions operations.

headlines.title: ICE agent's gun found in SFO bathroom
headlines.description: A flight attendant found an ICE agent’s gun unattended in a public restroom at San Francisco International Airport last month, NBC Bay Area’s Investigative Unit has confirmed. The gun was found in the stall of a men’s bathroom past the security checkpoint in Terminal 2 on the evening of July 21, according to SFO public information officer Doug Yakel. The flight attendant who found it reported the gun to security staff, who closed the restroom to the public and called 911, Yakel said in an email. San Francisco police officers responded within minutes and were on scene when the ICE officer later returned to retrieve the lost firearm, Yakel said. It’s still unclear how long the gun was left sitting in the bathroom before it was found. The airport reported the incident to TSA for potential follow-up action, Yakel added. It’s unclear what the ICE agent was doing at SFO or whether he has faced any discipline. Yakel said the airport wasn’t privy to the nature of ICE’s presence at the airport that evening, and ICE has not responded to questions sent Wednesday morning by NBC Bay Area. Ukrainian immigrant Iryna Gorb was arrested by ICE agents at SFO the following day. Video of her arrest was captured and posted online by Richmond city councilmember Doria Robinson. A Department of Homeland Security spokesperson said Gorb lawfully entered the U.S in 2010 but overstayed her visa by more than 15 years. NBC Bay Area’s Investigative Unit learned of the ICE agent’s lost gun through a public records request seeking further details on Gorb’s arrest. An internal email contained within a batch of records the airport released this week alluded to an “event where an ICE agent left his gun in the MRR near Checkpoint D in TB2.” The airport provided additional details Wednesday afternoon in response to questions from NBC Bay Area. ICE presence at U.S. airports has made headlines across the country in recent weeks, with immigration attorneys reporting an uptick in airport arrests and warning clients about flying. It’s unclear exactly how many immigrants have been arrested at SFO, but Yakel told NBC Bay Area the airport is aware of three such arrests since March, including the arrest of Gorb. Yakel said the airport is “not involved in decisions about DHS or ICE operations” and doesn’t “assist in immigration enforcement, consistent with Sanctuary City policies.” NBC Bay Area obtained CCTV footage of another such arrest on March 22 that also led to widespread public outcry after bystanders filmed the incident and posted it on social media. The third arrest took place on May 1, Yakel said. NBC Bay Area will update the story as we learn more.

headlines.title: Bodycam footage shows arrest of 49ers owner Jed York
headlines.description: Police body-camera video captured the moments when San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York was arrested in connection with an undercover prostitution bust. The arrest happened Sunday morning in East Palestine, Ohio. “Can I ask what you’re doing?” an officer can be heard saying in the video. “Just driving,” York responds. “You meeting anybody?” an officer asks. “No,” York responds. After placing York in the back of a police cruiser, officers searched his rental car and found cash totaling $160, which they say was the price he agreed to pay when he set up a sexual encounter with who he thought was a prostitute. York was arrested on suspicion of engaging in prostitution, but later pleaded no contest to lesser charges. York has been living in his hometown of Youngstown, Ohio, where his parents live, since filing for divorce earlier this year. His wife and two sons remain in Los Altos Hills. Jed York Aug 25 San Francisco 49ers Aug 24 49ers owner Jed York arrested in Ohio, pleads no contest to charges

headlines.title: ‘San Francisco, I choose you!': Businesses prepare for world's largest Pokémon competition
headlines.description: The Pokemon World Championships, the marquee tournament for people playing competitive Pokemon games, is coming to San Francisco this weekend with a prize of $2 million and the chance to win the title of “World Champion.” Thousands of people are expected to attend the tournament involving one of the world’s largest media franchises at San Francisco’s Moscone Center and Chase Center. Events and other festivities are planned Friday through Sunday for players of the video games, trading cards, Pokemon GO, and Pokemon UNITE. A $2 million prize pool is up for grabs, with players traveling from around the world after participating in competitions in their respective regions. People of all ages are expected to participate in the tournament, bringing together generations of fans who grew up wanting to “catch ’em all.” PokemonXP, a fan convention hosted by The Pokemon Company International, will be making its debut this year, as previous years of the world championships primarily focused on the tournament. Workshops, interactive experiences, and panels are a part of the jampacked agenda. San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie said the city is expecting more than 54,000 fans over the weekend, more than the 30,000 people who attended the previous year’s competition in Anaheim. He said on social media that a drone show is planned at the Ferry Building for Friday and Saturday at 9:35 p.m. and on Sunday at 9:20 p.m., free for everyone. “This event is bringing tens of thousands of visitors who will experience our neighborhoods, support our small businesses, and continue driving our comeback,” said Lurie on social media. “And the revenue they generate helps fund the services San Franciscans rely on every day across the city.” According to the event’s website, all tickets have been sold out for participants and attendees. Popup events throughout the city, including at Fisherman’s Wharf and Union Square, will help bring the Pokemon spirit to people not at the tournament sites. San Francisco has one of the two official Nintendo stores in the U.S. The other location is found in New York City, and it will be supporting the weekend events. The retailer is expecting to see elevated foot traffic at its location at Union Square in San Francisco as people flock to purchase merchandise and be a part of a franchise they care deeply about.
headlines.source: Andres Jimenez Larios | Bay City News

headlines.title: Roger Goodell says NFL is looking into whether to punish 49ers owner Jed York following his arrest
headlines.description: Commissioner Roger Goodell said the NFL is looking into whether San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York will be punished for violating the league’s personal conduct policy after he was caught in a prostitution sting in Ohio. “It’s being reviewed under the personal conduct policy,” Goodell said Wednesday at the owners’ meetings in Atlanta. “We’ll do that and when there’s something to be reported we’ll talk.” York was arrested in a mobile home park by the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force after police said he was attempting to pay $160 for sex with a woman he believed to be a prostitute. York was booked into jail and was released after posting a $5,000 bond. York was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct. He pleaded no contest to that charge and to possessing criminal tools for using his phone to respond to the an undercover online prostitution advertisement. He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offenses to be served concurrently and was credited with one day served when he pleaded no contest. He also was fined $1,150. Police seized the $160 from York and that was later given to the human trafficking task force as part of the plea. York also completed an online course. York has spent most of the summer in Ohio, where he grew up near Youngstown. He had filed for divorce from his wife, Danielle, in May, according to court records. Owners have been previously punished for violating the personal conduct policy. The late Indianapolis Colts owner Jim Irsay was suspended for six games and fined $500,000 following a guilty plea to driving while impaired in 2014. New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft was investigated but not punished by the league after he was arrested in Florida in 2019 for allegedly paying for sex with a woman at a massage parlor. The charge was later dropped after a court ruled that police violated the rights of Kraft and the other customers when they secretly installed video cameras inside massage rooms at the spa. York was arrested on Sunday in East Palestine, Ohio, and pleaded guilty on Monday to two misdemeanors. ___ AP Sports Writer Charles Odum in Atlanta contributed to this report. ___ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

headlines.title: 40-year-old man charged in deadly 2008 San Francisco shooting
headlines.description: A man has been charged in a deadly shooting that occurred more than 18 years ago in San Francisco, prosecutors said Thursday. Derreyl Chase Goode, 40, was charged with murder in connection with a fatal shooting that occurred in April 2008. He also faces an allegation that he used a firearm in the commission of the murder, the San Francisco District Attorney’s Office said in a statement. According to court documents, on April 27, 2008, San Francisco officers responded to 520 Fulton St. regarding a shooting. They found a victim lying on the ground with an apparent gunshot wound to the face. Witnesses alleged Goode was seen standing over the victim as the victim’s body hit the ground. The victim was later identified by the San Francisco Medical Examiner’s Office as 28-year-old Jason Mosley. “After a substantial investigation by SFPD, Mr. Goode was arrested,” the department said. Goode was expected to be arraigned Thursday morning. Anyone with relevant information is asked to call the department’s Tip Line at 1-415-575-4444 or text a tip to TIP411 and begin the text message with “SFPD”.

headlines.title: Oakland's Chabot Space and Science Center to host lunar eclipse watch party
headlines.description: Bay Area residents will have a chance to watch a partial lunar eclipse Thursday night, weather permitting, at the Chabot Space & Science Center in Oakland. The center will start hosting the lunar eclipse watch party at 7 p.m. at its facility at 10000 Skyline Blvd. as the moon passes into Earth’s shadow. The partial eclipse is expected to begin at 7:33 p.m., with the eclipse reaching its maximum at 9:12 p.m., according to the event information.

headlines.title: What we know about the changes Meta will roll out for teens and parents
headlines.description: Wednesday, Facebook and Instagram’s parent company, Meta, announced it had reached a settlement with the attorneys general from across the country (including California) in the social media addiction lawsuit playing out in an Oakland courtroom. As part of the settlement, Meta agreed to pay out around $18 billion to the states involved and to make changes to its apps. Based on the details of the settlement, the first of those changes are set to roll out in a matter of months, others will take more than a year. The changes for users under 18 include: Two-hour daily limits for use which teens will need parents’ permission to turn off Blocking Meta apps from midnight to 6 a.m. Stronger age verification measures Hiding the number of likes or reactions on posts Blocking teens from using what Meta calls “extreme makeup filters” Muting notifications from 8 a.m. to 3 p.m. for “school mode” Sending prompts to teens after 15 minutes of continuous screentime on Instagram and Facebook Allowing teens to choose a non-algorithmic feed Allowing teens to turn off the autoplay setting Adding new parental controls like telling parents when a teen links a secondary account to their app or interacts with an account that is potentially suspicious Meta also said it’s working to catch and remove underage accounts on their apps and find accounts that may belong to people younger than 13. “The framework we’ve negotiated will empower parents to easily manage how their children access our platforms,” said C.J. Mahoney, Meta’s Chief Legal Officer, in a prepared video statement. The settlement states that within one year, Meta must adopt an “age assurance framework” which must be tested annually by an accredited third party. Within six months, Meta is expected to roll out efforts to detect users under the age of 13. Within four months, Meta is required to implement pauses after they have been using Meta apps continuously for more than 15 minutes and when their total daily usage hits 60 minutes and 90 minutes “to encourage intentional use.” Tech and legal experts say questions remain about how Meta will verify a user’s age without creating new privacy concerns. “The industry was not really very serious about it for a long time, 20 years,” said Ahmed Banafa, Professor of Engineering at San Jose State. Banafa said from a technical standpoint, he expects the age verification measures to be the most difficult parts of the agreement for Meta to fulfill. He explained the debate about how to do this has been “between privacy and protection.” Some legal experts say that is a difficult balance to strike. Nora Benavidez, Senior Counsel at the organization Free Press, has been following this case and noted, “I think one of my other biggest concerns and outstanding questions is about children and their safety and parents’ decisions about how much information they will have to give over to prove the children’s age.” Benavidez wondered how many users across the impacted states will be required to share personal data including age with Meta under these changes. “These are going to be very complicated months ahead,” Benavidez said of the expected rollout of these changes, adding that “parents have a tremendous role right now, in this very uncertain and contentious period.” Alyssa Goard has the full report in the video above.
